item: Deeper study — the devout daily reader (deeper_study)
angle: The passage is the product. Every study tool goes one tap behind it, the plan day is the only number on screen, and the app asks this reader exactly one question, once.
thesis: This reader already has the habit; what the app owes them is the text, dated, at the top, in under three seconds. Today it does the opposite. On day 0 they are asked to choose a plan three separate times on one screen with no scripture anywhere on it (the hero funnel at HomeScreen.tsx:2208-2240, the two-step wizard at PastorStudyOnboarding.tsx:269-329, and the "No reading plan active" card at HomeScreen.tsx:3512-3531). From day 1 on, the chapter does arrive already open — which is right and stays — but it arrives wrapped in a control deck (chapter pills, Stop/Read, Restart, N translation chips, Compare, then N more compare chips) with a pre-expanded commentary card and a second copy of the same chapter below it under "TODAY'S STUDY", because heroChapterRefs and todaysPlanPassages both start from the same plan passage (HomeScreen.tsx:1291-1296 vs 3250). That is precisely the complaint the research records against the category leader: "it keeps adding functionality, it's getting so cluttered." The design keeps everything Ashley has locked — the white paper hero, the Georgia serif, the credit-free arrival seed, the bright editorial plate — and takes three things away from the screen and one away from the logic: the duplicate chapter card, the always-open commentary, the scattered depth chips (all three move behind one "Study" tap on the passage), and the silent plan credit that fires just because you expanded a chapter. It adds two things: a single day-0 question with three answers that resolves in one tap, and a done state that is filled and live rather than a greyed-out disabled button. Richer, not stripped: the passage gets the whole panel, a real plan line, provenance on every commentary, and a paper mode for the 89% who still prefer print.
principles: Text first, tools on tap. Commentary, Compare and original languages collapse behind one "Study" control on the passage. Source: Persona 3, "Commentary, Compare and original languages collapse behind one 'Study' tap (they are open by default today)" and "the recurring YouVersion complaint is 'it keeps adding functionality, it's getting so cluttered'."
A dated plan is the spine, and it is the only progress number on the screen. Source: Persona 3, "Day 0: choose a plan... Dated, resumable" and "3M+ one-year plan starts on 1 Jan 2025, +18% YoY."

One question, three answers, one tap. The tap starts the plan AND opens today's chapter in place — never a confirmation screen, never a CTA below the fold. Source: Persona 3 "two or three at most"; ruling project_daily_word_choose_your_path line 87 ("Tapping a card must save AND open the screen immediately... no separate CTA below the fold").
Audio belongs on the passage, not in its own section. Source: Persona 3, "Audio as a companion, on the passage, not in a separate section (Dwell)."

Completion is deliberate. Expanding a chapter is not reading it. Source: the repo's own settled position at HomeScreen.tsx:713-716 ("Replaces auto-marking on open (focus-group: completion needs intent)"), which handleRead at :754-755 still contradicts; and the ruling that the arrival seed must be credit-free.

No shame, ever, in a number. A missed day offers two live choices, not an apology. Source: cross-cutting finding 6, "Streaks work until they shame... guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall," plus Persona 3, "a reset without shame."

Paper is the reference standard, not a novelty. Source: Persona 3, "89% of Bible users still prefer print; 55% use a smartphone" → "a 'read like paper' mode, larger type, no chrome"; and Ashley's locked white hero panel as deliberate "paper mode."
Nothing greyed and nothing asked twice. Every control on screen is live; anything the app can compute (the day number, the reminder hour, which study tab you last used) is never a question.

journey.day0: They tap "Going deeper" in the one path sheet and land on Home. One question — "Where are you reading?" — with three dated plans under it. No wizard, no funnel hero, no "No reading plan active" card. One tap starts the plan, and today's chapter opens in the same block without navigating. Total asks on day 0: one, down from three.
journey.first_session: The chapter fills the white paper panel under a plan line that reads "Through the Bible in a Year · Day 1 of 365". Three controls above the text: Listen, Study, Paper. They tap Study once out of curiosity, see Commentary with its source line, close it. They write one line into Reflect. They tap Mark as read and the button becomes a filled row: "Day 1 of 365 done." The quiet DoneCelebration shows once.
journey.return_visit: They open the app; the chapter for today is already expanded and loaded before they touch anything (the existing credit-free arrival seed at HomeScreen.tsx:1449-1456, unchanged). Greeting names the day. Same three controls. Nothing on the screen has moved since yesterday.
journey.week2: The plan line reads "Day 12 of 365". The done row gains a second line computed from the plan itself: "Five of the last seven days." The Study sheet opens on whichever tab they used last. Around session seven, the Reminders card in More offers the hour they actually open the app, once, in neutral words — never a streak threat.
journey.missed_day: Two days missed. No red, no badge, no apology copy. Above the panel, one line — "You were on Day 12." — and two live buttons: "Pick up at Day 12" and "Jump to today, Day 15." Whichever they tap, the chapter opens. The reminder card never mentions the gap.
journey.seasonal: A dated Futures series plan appears as a fourth row in the plan picker and on the Plans tab during the season, and nowhere else — no interstitial, no takeover of the opening screen. Calendar moments are where the spikes come from (cross-cutting finding 5), but for this persona they arrive as a plan they can choose, not as an interruption to a reading in progress.

comfort_access: One line at the foot of Home on this path, present every day, never a badge and never an interstitial: "Hard day? The comfort readings are here." It opens the comfort reading as a sub-view over Home (useSubView alone) and closes back to the same scroll position. It must not call saveSetup, must not write dw_setup, must not stamp a source, must not credit dw_reading_done and must not touch the streak — a bad day is not a path change, and only onboarding/settings/upgrade count as a real choice. Inside it, the toolbar is Note and Close only, and there is no graduation prompt, no "feeling stronger?", no return path suggestion — that prompt was removed for good and is never re-added. Source: cross-cutting research, "From every path: a persistent one-tap 'I need comfort now' that opens comfort without switching the saved path. Crisis is not a persona someone chooses on a good day"; rulings on comfortMode toolbar, the removed graduation prompt, and saveSetup's source gate.
reminders: One a day, at the hour behaviour says they read, in neutral words. The offer appears once, after seven sessions, with the inferred hour already filled in and one tap to accept; before that the manual picker is the only thing on the card. Nothing in the push copy, the card copy or the app ever frames a missed day as a loss — no "your streak is about to die", no fire emoji on this path, no catch-up guilt. Source: cross-cutting finding 6 ("one nudge a day, timed to when the person actually last opened (Duolingo's behaviour-inferred timing)... guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall") and Persona 2's reminder line, which the research applies across paths. Operational constraint from the rulings: pushSupported() allowlists only futuresdailyword.com, www and localhost, so the reminder work is verified on localhost or on prod after merge — never on the deploy preview Ashley is looking at. Say that in the PR so the preview is judged on layout and copy, not on push.
instrumentation: plan_start with detail "<planId>|day0-card" vs "|plans-tab" — proves the single day-0 question converts better than today's three asks. Already in the TRACKED_EVENTS allowlist; only the detail changes.
reading_done with detail "<planId>|<dayNum>" — the deliberate Mark as read. New event; this is the only honest completion signal once handleRead stops crediting.

study_open with detail "<chapterRef>|<firstTab>" — how often the collapsed depth layer is actually wanted. New. The research's own test for this persona is session length and 30-day retention with Study collapsed vs open.
study_tab with detail "commentary|compare|greek|xref" — which tool earns its tab. New.
paper_mode with detail "<chapterRef>" — validates the 89%-prefer-print move or kills it. New.
comfort_peek with detail "deeper_study" — reach of the comfort tap from this path, and confirmation it never changes the saved persona. New.
reminder_set with detail "<hour>|inferred" or "<hour>|manual", and push_unsubscribe — acceptance of the inferred hour, and opt-out as the guard rail on all reminder copy.
offline_read with detail "<chapterRef>|<servedTranslation>" — how often the KJV fallback is doing the work, which decides whether ESV caching is worth building.
path on every event. Add it alongside campus in gaEvent's params (analytics.ts:22-28) and to the Supabase activity detail, or none of the above can be cut by persona — which is the whole point.
D1 / D7 / D30 by path, session length and completion rate, as one nightly rollup. Research build priority 1: no public source will ever supply this, and every claim above is untestable without it.
self_serve_levers: Exists today — src/data/commentary.ts: add a passage/source key to the COMMENTARY object to extend curated coverage. Plain data, no component logic. This is the highest-value lever for a campus pastor: it replaces an AI Insight with a real commentary on any chapter they care about.

Exists today — src/data/plans.ts: plan entries, passages and totalDays. Adding a dated Futures series plan for a season is a data edit here plus one id in the persona list. Trap: a plan id is referenced in four places (personalization.ts, SetupPromptModal.tsx, PlansScreen.tsx, PastorStudyOnboarding.tsx) and all four must be rewired or the wizard starts a dead plan.

Exists today — src/utils/persona-config.ts:380-429, the deeper_study block: sectionOrder, the features flags, plans.featuredCategories and ai.systemPromptAddition are all plain data fields. The AI's scholarly instruction for this path is editable here without touching a component.
Exists today — src/utils/i18n.ts: every string on every screen above. New keys go here with es/pt/id alongside; translated content is Claude-drafted and Ashley approves before ship.
Exists today — netlify/functions/strongs.js:5-27: the COMMON_NT / COMMON_OT inline dictionaries take new key/value entries; anything else falls through to the external Open Scriptures API.

Worth building, small — the three day-0 plan ids and their one-line descriptions as a single row per campus, served through the existing user-sync/Supabase layer and cached locally, editable from the admin dashboard that already exists. That is the one change that takes "which three plans do we recommend" out of the repo entirely. Everything else on this list is a file edit that deploys on merge — honest, but not self-serve.

open_decisions: The three day-0 plans and their order. Proposed: Through the Bible in a Year, New Testament in 90 Days, Psalms & Proverbs — all three already in this persona's five, so nothing new enters the catalogue. Confirm or reorder.

Whether "read with" is built at all — one reading partner, both seeing a day-count and nothing else. The research argues for it from the 24% → 13% collapse in weekly Bible-study group participation; it is the only social feature proposed on this path, and the research itself lists it as your call.
Whether a dated Futures series plan joins the day-0 three during a season, or lives only on the Plans tab.

Whether the AI Insight commentary fallback should exist on this path at all, given this is the reader most likely to check a source. Options: keep it labelled as designed, restrict it to chapters with no curated entry (today's behaviour), or hide it here and show "No commentary for this chapter yet."
Whether the commentary provenance line shows the licence ("public domain") to readers or only the source name.
risks: This is a big IA reshape of the opening screen for one persona, which is the exact class of change that was reverted on 1 Sep as "completely stripped". It must not merge without Ashley's word on a deploy preview. The countermeasure inside the design: nothing is deleted, it is relocated one tap deep, and the passage gets bigger and warmer as a result — full-height paper panel, a real plan line, provenance on the commentary, a paper mode. If the preview reads as thin, the fix is more warmth on the panel, not putting the chips back on top.

Removing the plan credit from handleRead changes completion semantics for congregation and pastor_leader too, not just this path. It is a correctness fix against the code's own stated intent, but it belongs in its own commit with its own line in the PR body and its own test, so it can be reverted alone.
If HomeScreen is ever re-extracted or retired as part of this work, the ten src/sections/* files and their tests must come back with it. That is a ruling, and it is the trap that bit last time.

The Study sheet and Paper mode are nested overlays over a screen that already hosts BibleAI. Use useSubView alone — no useModalA11y, no aria-modal — and mount them with a live open prop rather than conditionally, or Android back and the keyboard path break in ways that only show up on a phone.

Leaving 'plan_scripture' in sectionOrder is load-bearing in two places: the generic "Choose Your Plan" button at HomeScreen.tsx:2854 gates on its absence, and PastorStudyOnboarding mounts on its presence at :2879. Remove the key and both regress.

PastorStudyOnboarding is shared with pastor_leader. Only the !isPastor branches (lines 269-298 and the step-2 picker at 300-328 when reached from step 0 !isPastor) may be removed; the pastor wizard stays whole.

Push cannot be verified on the deploy preview — pushSupported() allowlists prod and localhost only. Verify reminders on localhost before the PR and on prod after merge, and say so in the PR so the preview is not judged on it.

No /books/* or /bible/* content changes are needed for this work. If any land alongside it, bump CACHE_NAME, STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION together, and never reuse a bundled image filename — both are recorded traps.

Any new synced dw_* field must merge into what is currently in localStorage and touch only its own fields, never be rebuilt from React state. The design deliberately avoids new synced storage — "five of the last seven days" is computed from the plan's existing completedDays through calcPlanDay's local-date axis, and no UTC date logic enters anywhere near plan day.
